<submission>
**Recurrent orthostatic headache with persistent lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis and meningeal signs following suspected aseptic meningitis.**

**Intracranial hypotension from CSF leak (post-LP).** The orthostatic pattern, worse upright and relieved by lying flat, is the hallmark. Multiple lumbar punctures were performed during this admission. Limitation: no imaging specifically targeting a leak (contrast-enhanced MRI or CT myelogram) is reported. Next: contrast-enhanced brain MRI to look for pachymeningeal enhancement; consider CT myelogram if confirmed.

**Persistent aseptic meningitis.** Repeat CSF still shows 178 cells/µL, 97.7% lymphocytes, with ongoing meningeal signs and photophobia. PCR was negative, but no CSF culture result is supplied, so an infectious aetiology is not fully excluded. Next: CSF culture, broader PCR panel, and serum autoimmune encephalitis antibodies.

**Post-infectious or autoimmune meningeal inflammation.** The febrile prodrome, lymphocytic pleocytosis, negative infectious workup, and persistence despite nine days of dexamethasone raise this possibility. Limitation: no autoimmune or specific serology is reported. Next: ANA, anti-aquaporin-4, anti-NMDAR antibodies in serum and CSF.

**Reassessment before management:** Confirm the orthostatic pattern on examination, document whether an epidural blood patch has been performed, and obtain current neurological status including fundoscopy.
</submission>
